page.layout: One page of text: a Latin verse poem set in italic, followed at the right by the catchword "SYNTA-", with a woodcut ornament below the text.

p.i: Sic nunc Musarum (concedunt numina) fontes Nectare abundantes ambrosiaq; fluunt: Utq; breui spacio, facilíq; labore medullam, Cordaq; Pieridum tangere & ossa queas. Huc igitur Tyro docilis properato: benignæ Et citò, quæ Musæ dona dedêre, cape. Laus iam sit superis, laus Musis, lausq; perennis Authori, hoc fœlix qui benè scripsit opus. Revera is merito non est indignus honore. Quem benè de studiis tu meruisse vides. Vivat Bolstenius, duretq; ad Nestoris annos Hoc opus, & fructu numina sancta beent.

page.notes: Woodcut ornament (floral/scroll motif) centred below the text; not transcribed. Faint show-through of the reverse side is visible in the lower half and was left out. "Bolstenius" is read with some doubt from the scan. Long s is printed as s and given as s. No page number or running head is printed.
